Download every sub-theme of a UKHSA dashboard theme

Source: R/subthemes.R
get_subtheme_data.Rd

Runs get_data once per sub-theme (all topics, all geographies and all metrics at one geography type) and optionally saves each result to its own file. With the defaults it retrieves the ten sub-themes of infectious_disease (antimicrobial resistance, bloodborne, bloodstream infection, childhood illness, contact, gastrointestinal, invasive bacterial infections, respiratory, vaccine-preventable and vector-borne).

Usage

get_subtheme_data(
  sub_themes = NULL,
  theme = "infectious_disease",
  topic = "*",
  geography_type = NULL,
  geography = "*",
  metric = "*",
  out_dir = NULL,
  format = c("csv", "csv.gz", "rds"),
  as_data_table = FALSE,
  max_datasets = 1e+05,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

sub_themes

character vector of sub-themes. NULL (default) means the ten known infectious_disease sub-themes. Values containing * or ? are expanded against the API, so "*" fetches every sub-theme the API lists for theme.

theme

the theme, default "infectious_disease".

topic, geography, metric

passed to get_data; all default to "*" (everything).

geography_type

the geography type to retrieve. NULL (default) uses "Nation" for the contact and vector_borne sub-themes, which are only published nationally, and "UKHSA Region" for everything else. Supply a single value to use for all sub-themes, or a named vector (e.g. c(respiratory = "Nation")) to override individual sub-themes.

out_dir

optional directory. If supplied, each sub-theme is saved as <out_dir>/<sub_theme>.<format>.

format

file format used when out_dir is supplied: "csv" (default), "csv.gz" or "rds".

as_data_table

if TRUE, return data.tables rather than data.frames.

max_datasets

passed to get_data; the per-sub-theme safety limit on the number of metric datasets. The default is generous because a whole sub-theme can contain thousands of datasets.

verbose

show progress messages.

Value

A named list with one element per sub-theme: a data.frame (or data.table), or NULL if that sub-theme could not be retrieved. Returns NULL invisibly if sub_themes contained patterns that could not be resolved.

Details

This is a large download, issued at the rate set by options(ukhsadatR.requests_per_second = ) (default one request per second), so it takes a long time. Preview a single sub-theme's size first with get_combinations, and use sub_themes to fetch only what you need. Sub-themes that fail to resolve or download are skipped with a message, and the rest are still returned.

See also

get_data, get_combinations

Examples

# \donttest{
# Two sub-themes only, kept in memory
x <- get_subtheme_data(sub_themes = c("contact", "vector_borne"))
#> == infectious_disease / contact (Nation) ==
#> Looking up geography types for 3 combinations...
#> Looking up geographies for 3 combinations...
#> Looking up metrics for 3 combinations...
#> Downloading 3 datasets (at least 3 requests; ~1 min at 1 request(s)/sec)...
#> [1/3] mpox | England | mpox_cases_countByMonth
#> [2/3] mpox-clade-1b | England | mpox-clade-1b_cases_countByMonth
#> [3/3] mpox-clade-2b | England | mpox-clade-2b_cases_countByMonth
#> == infectious_disease / vector_borne (Nation) ==
names(x)
#> [1] "contact"      "vector_borne"

# The respiratory sub-theme by nation rather than region, saved to disk
get_subtheme_data(
  sub_themes = "respiratory",
  geography_type = "Nation",
  out_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "ukhsa")
)
